expected.title: Reading Travel Conditions
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Reading Travel Conditions.

Seafaring needs knowledge of water, weather, routes and the boat. People learned through experience and teaching.

Winds and currents can affect a journey. A planned route may need to change when conditions change.

Careful preparation reduces risks but cannot promise a safe trip in every situation.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Check the boat; Check water and weather; Adjust the plan. Preparation can reduce risk; it cannot promise every journey is safe.

expected.title: Why People Exchanged Goods
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Why People Exchanged Goods.

Communities had different resources and skills. Exchange could help people obtain useful or valued goods.

People also made things locally. Trading did not mean all communities stopped farming, fishing or crafting.

Goods could serve daily needs, ceremonies or social purposes. We should check evidence rather than assume one purpose.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Local resources and skills; Useful or valued goods; Exchange and local work. Exchange did not mean that all local production stopped.
fields.imageCaption: Modern teaching diagram based on this lesson, not an original historical image.

expected.title: Reading Routes Carefully
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Reading Routes Carefully.

Maps of past trade are explanations based on evidence. They are not photographs of every ship journey.

Researchers use objects, written accounts and other sources together. Each source has limits.

Modern country names can help us locate places today, but past borders and communities were different.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Objects and accounts; Compare dated evidence; Explain a possible route. A route explanation is not a record of every ship journey.
fields.imageCaption: Modern teaching diagram based on this lesson, not an original historical image.

expected.title: Useful and Valued Goods
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Useful and Valued Goods.

Goods could meet different needs. Pots could hold things, while cloth could have everyday and social uses.

The same object may have different uses in different settings. Look for clues rather than guess.

Local goods and imported goods could both be valued.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Object; Setting and evidence; Supported use. The same kind of object can have different uses in different settings.

expected.title: Ideas Travel Too
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Ideas Travel Too.

People meeting through travel could share language, skills and beliefs. Cultural exchange can move in more than one direction.

A community may change a borrowed idea to suit its needs. Not every group accepts the same ideas.

Sharing is not proof that one society had no ideas of its own.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. People meet; Ideas are shared; Communities make choices. Ideas can move in more than one direction; acceptance is not automatic.
fields.imageCaption: Modern teaching diagram based on this lesson, not an original historical image.

expected.title: People Behind the Exchange
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: People Behind the Exchange.

Maritime communities needed more than visiting merchants. Boatbuilders, food producers and skilled makers could support daily life and exchange.

Different responsibilities could connect people without giving them equal rights or power.

A list of goods alone may not name all the people whose work supported trade.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Boatbuilders; Food producers; Skilled makers. Different work could support exchange without equal power for everyone.
fields.imageCaption: Modern teaching diagram based on this lesson, not an original historical image.

expected.title: Trading Places Change
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Trading Places Change.

Routes and trading places could change over time. Environmental conditions, relationships and needs affected connections.

Evidence from one period cannot automatically describe the same place in every century.

Researchers compare dated finds to explain change rather than assume a place was always the same.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Evidence from one period; Evidence from another; Compare what changed. One dated find does not describe every century.
fields.imageCaption: Modern teaching diagram based on this lesson, not an original historical image.

expected.title: More Than One Way to Communicate
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: More Than One Way to Communicate.

People communicated through spoken language, stories, signs and writing. Different forms could serve different purposes.

A written object and an oral account are different kinds of sources. Each needs careful study.

The absence of a surviving written record does not prove that a community had no knowledge or history.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Spoken accounts; Signs and writing; Study each source. No surviving written record does not mean no knowledge or history.

expected.title: Writing Traditions Continue
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Writing Traditions Continue.

The National Museum presents continuing script traditions among communities including Hanunoo, Buhid, Tagbanua and Pala'wan. These names should not be treated as interchangeable.

Present-day community members are people with choices, not examples frozen in the past.

Learning respectfully means using reliable sources and respecting how communities describe their own knowledge.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Distinct community names; Continuing traditions; Community knowledge. Hanunoo, Buhid, Tagbanua and Pala'wan are not interchangeable names.

expected.title: Skilled Work Is Technology
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Skilled Work Is Technology.

Technology is not limited to electric devices. Pottery, carving and boatbuilding involve methods and tools.

A maker chooses techniques for a purpose and learns through practice and teaching.

Careful study should not rank a community as less capable because its tools differ from modern ones.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Purpose; Methods and tools; Practice and teaching. Technology includes skilled methods, not only electric devices.
fields.imageCaption: Modern teaching diagram based on this lesson, not an original historical image.

expected.title: Designs Need Context
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Designs Need Context.

Designs can have meanings connected with community practices. Not every pattern has the same meaning or is free to copy.

A responsible learner checks how a design is described and whether its use has restrictions.

A classroom activity can explore general making skills without copying sacred or restricted designs.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Identify the source; Understand the context; Check permitted use. Explore general making skills without copying restricted designs.
fields.imageCaption: Modern teaching diagram based on this lesson, not an original historical image.

expected.title: Surroundings and Human Choices
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Surroundings and Human Choices.

Surroundings can influence available materials and activities. People also make choices and learn from others.

A coastal location does not mean everyone has the same livelihood or belief. Environment alone cannot explain a whole culture.

Understanding a practice needs local evidence and the people's knowledge.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Available materials; People make choices; Investigate local evidence. Environment alone does not explain a whole culture.

expected.title: Listen to Shared Knowledge
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Listen to Shared Knowledge.

Stories, songs and spoken accounts can carry knowledge and memories. Communities may have rules about who can share some material.

A tradition should be identified and understood in its own setting. A fictional classroom story is not automatically an authentic community tradition.

Respectful study asks about source, meaning and limits.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Who shares the account?; What is its setting?; What may be shared?. A fictional classroom story is not an authentic community tradition.

expected.title: Shared Identity, Different Experiences
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Shared Identity, Different Experiences.

People may share a Filipino identity while belonging to different communities and traditions. Shared identity does not require sameness in every practice.

The people of the precolonial islands did not all use a single modern national identity in the way we do today.

We can value their contributions without treating the past as identical to the present.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Shared identity; Different communities; Different experiences. Modern shared identity does not make the past identical to the present.

expected.title: Caring Is Part of Learning
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Caring Is Part of Learning.

Heritage care includes protecting objects, places and knowledge. Communities have important roles in deciding how their traditions are shared.

Useful actions include following site rules, crediting sources and asking permission when needed.

Respect does not mean taking objects home or publishing everything that can be recorded.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

fields.imageAlt: Modern learning diagram. Follow site rules; Credit sources; Ask permission when needed. Caring does not mean taking objects or publishing everything recorded.
